results.title: Apple responds to user reports of broken iPhone Duo screens
results.content:
In this article

Apple's first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo, hit store shelves on Friday to considerable lines and long wait times for preorders.

But some customers who were lucky enough to get the $1,999-and-up phone on its first weekend have been reporting a pretty big problem: The inner screen of the phone can break, showing horizontal bright lines emanating from the phone's hinge.

Apple on Monday said that it was aware of the issue, which it said affected a "small number" of phones, and that it would replace the devices under its AppleCare warranty. [...] "We are aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units," an Apple representative told CNBC. "If users experience issues with their iPhone Duo display, they should contact AppleCare for a replacement."

Apple says on its website that an inner-screen repair will be $999 for iPhone Duos that are out of warranty.

Most of the reports are from anonymous customers on online forums such as Reddit and X, and there are fake images online as well. But well-respected device repair firm iFixit weighed in on Sunday, after tearing down the new device and testing its resistance to dust, and theorized the issues may have to do with Apple's hinge design. [...] Early reviewers praised the experience of using the iPhone Duo when unfolded, especially for multitasking or media, but said that many apps had not been updated to take full advantage of the phone's larger and wider screens.

Apple said Monday that apps were already being updated for the new foldable device.

"The response to iPhone Duo from early users has been incredibly positive, and we are seeing exciting things from developers who are rapidly updating their apps to take advantage of its unique form factor," an Apple representative said in a statement.
